title: Quiz: Process Variation — Sources and Types

questions.text: A process is said to be 'in statistical control' when:
options: No variation of any kind is present
All measurements fall within specification limits
Special-cause variation is less than 5% of total variation
questions.explanation: Statistical control means the process is stable and predictable — only common-cause (random, inherent) variation is present. Specification limits are a separate concept from control limits.

questions.text: Which of the 6M categories best describes a root cause of 'incorrect SQL query algorithm deployed to production'?
questions.explanation: Method covers procedures, algorithms, and how work is done. A wrong query algorithm is a Method issue — the process of doing the work was incorrect.

questions.text: A run chart shows 9 consecutive data points all above the historical median. This is best interpreted as:
options: A process shift — likely a special cause
Evidence that the median was computed incorrectly
Insufficient data to draw any conclusion
questions.explanation: 8 or more consecutive points on the same side of the median is a standard run chart signal for a process shift — the probability of this occurring by chance from a stable process is very low.

questions.text: A data engineer notices that ETL batch runtimes have been gradually increasing for 7 consecutive days. In run chart terms, this pattern is called a:
questions.explanation: A trend is 6 or more consecutive points steadily moving in one direction (all increasing or all decreasing). This suggests a gradual drift in the process — perhaps accumulating data volume or slow memory leak.

questions.text: Treating common-cause variation as if it were special-cause variation and making adjustments will typically reduce process variation.
questions.explanation: Adjusting a stable process in response to what is actually random noise is called 'over-adjustment' or 'tampering.' It adds extra variation on top of the existing natural variation, making the process worse — not better. This is Deming's funnel experiment result.
